Sofia —

Thanks for the materials so far. As we begin to consolidate vendor responses for the AI governance section of our RFP, a few clarifications would help our internal review team (security + regulatory + procurement):

1) NIST AI RMF mapping: can you provide a succinct mapping (controls -> product features) showing how Redwood implements Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Govern? We need to surface concrete artifacts we can request during due diligence (e.g., dataset provenance export, model provenance, access control logs).

2) EU AI Act: our use-case (clinical decision support triage) is likely to be considered high-risk. Can Redwood outline the practical deployment options you support for high-risk systems (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and any role you can play in pre-market conformity assessment (e.g., evidence packages, support for third-party assessors)?

3) Continuous regression and evaluation: we're asking for your sampling approach, baseline construction, drift detection windows, and typical acceptance thresholds for regression. We need to understand both automated checks and when you recommend human-driven review.

4) Evidence & artifacts: please indicate what attachments you can provide quickly (SOC 2 type II, data retention policy, sample eval reports, test harness config) and an expected ETA to deliver those.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30‑minute sync this week with our legal/regulatory lead.

Best,
Samir Desai
Head of Vendor Risk — Helion Health

Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; we’ll attach the artifacts you asked for and propose a short mutual action plan at the end.

1) NIST AI RMF mapping (summary)
- Identify: model & dataset cataloging (artifacted model manifests, dataset lineage IDs, ingestion timestamps).
- Protect: RBAC, per-route tenant isolation, encryption in transit/at rest (KMS/HSM integrations).
- Detect: automated drift and distribution monitors, anomaly alerting, request/response anomaly scoring (latency and semantic deviation).
- Respond: rollback & canary mechanisms, incident playbooks, forensic export of requests (redacted) for postmortem.
- Govern: policy engine for routing/labels, changelogs for model rollouts, eval/regression records linked to releases.

Artifacts you can request quickly: model-provenance export (csv), access-log extracts, SOC 2 Type II report, and our governance matrix. We will attach a concise mapping doc titled "redwood-nist-eu-mapping.pdf" with control pointers to product features.

2) EU AI Act — high-risk scenarios
- Classification: Redwood does not make a legal determination but provides the artifacts you need to assess classification. For clinical decision support we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment modes to minimize third‑party access risk and to support customer-led conformity assessment.
- Role in conformity: we provide a configurable evidence bundle (technical documentation, risk assessment templates, evaluation reports, and traceability exports) that customers can use in conformity assessment. For customers selecting Private deployment we can also coordinate with your assessor on system architecture and provide operational evidence under NDAs.

3) Continuous regression & evaluation approach
- Baselines: production-sampled prompts + curated seed prompt sets (customer + vendor curated).
- Sampling: hybrid stratified sampling by route, intent, and model confidence; typical sample windows are 24–72 hours for latency-sensitive flows, and 7–14 days for lower-frequency heavy prompts.
- Metrics: semantic similarity to baseline (embedding-based), hallucination/precision rate (task-specific checklists), toxicity/offensiveness scores, latency percentiles, and user-level business metrics where available.
- Acceptance thresholds: configurable per-account; default conservative thresholds: semantic-similarity delta < 0.08 (cosine-based), hallucination increase < 1.5% absolute, toxicity delta < 0.2%.
- Human-in-the-loop: automated alerts surface candidate regressions; customers define escalations to human review and can mark prompt-sets for manual sampling.

4) Evidence ETA
- SOC 2 Type II summary: available now (we will attach the certified summary).
- Sample eval reports & harness config: 48–72 hours to produce a de-identified example (we will attach "eval-regression-sampling-plan.xlsx").

Next steps / offer
- I’ve cc’d Aditya (infrastructure/product) and Marcus (legal/regulatory). Proposed 30‑minute sync on Fri 6 Aug at 10:00 PT to walk you through the mapping doc and sample eval. If that works, we’ll also upload the one‑page governance appendix and the export artifacts to a secure share.

Attachments (initial): redwood-nist-eu-mapping.pdf, governance-appendix-one-pager.pdf

Samir / team —

Two quick technical notes to complement Sofia’s answers:

- Rollouts & rollbacks: our runtime supports staged rollouts (canary by request hash, A/B by tenant, % rollout) and an automated rollback trigger when key telemetry exceeds configured thresholds. Rollbacks include a model-id pin and immutable changelog so you always have a reproducible rollback point.

- Fallbacks: for safety-critical flows we recommend enabling automatic fallback to a conservative, smaller model variant (lower creativity/temperature) when confidence or safety filters fail. This minimizes disruption while protecting against severe hallucination spikes.

- Auditability: per-request KV cache traces and token-level logs (configurable TTL) can be exported for assessor review. We can redact PHI in exports depending on your policy.

If you want a sample policy for triggers we can attach a short SOP and an example thresholds file.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
VP, Product — Redwood Inference
